links.title: Mastering Bitcoin, 3rd edition - Chapter 6: Transactions (the book's source, CC BY-SA 4.0)
links.why: The chapter itself, free to read: every quotation in this page is re-read from the commit the textbook ontology pins.

links.title: BIP 141: Segregated Witness (Consensus layer) (status: Deployed)
links.why: Defines the witness-independent txid, the wtxid, the witness program template, weight as base size times three plus total size, and the 4,000,000 block weight limit this page recomputes.

links.title: BIP 144: Segregated Witness (Peer Services) (status: Deployed)
links.why: The extended serialization format: the zero marker, the 0x01 flag read as a bit vector, and the witness structure at the end of the transaction.

links.title: BIP 68: Relative lock-time using consensus-enforced sequence numbers (status: Deployed)
links.why: The third meaning of the sequence field, bit by bit: the disable flag, the type flag at 1 << 22, the 16-bit mask and the 512-second units this page decodes.

links.title: BIP 112: CHECKSEQUENCEVERIFY (status: Deployed)
links.why: The opcode, deployed with BIP68, that lets an output script demand a relative timelock and fails in a transaction below version 2.

links.title: BIP 113: Median time-past as endpoint for lock-time calculations (status: Deployed)
links.why: Why a time lock is compared with the median of eleven block times rather than with a block's own timestamp.

links.title: BIP 125: Opt-in Full Replace-by-Fee Signaling (status: Deployed)
links.why: The signal of a sequence below 0xfffffffe, the rules a replacement must meet, and inherited signalling.

links.title: BIP 431: Topology Restrictions for Pinning (status: Draft)
links.why: The version 3 proposal the chapter says was being considered: a relay policy, not a consensus change, implemented by Bitcoin Core since 28.0.

links.title: BIP 174: Partially Signed Bitcoin Transaction Format (status: Deployed)
links.why: The only other widely used serialization: the magic bytes, the maps and the roles that pass a transaction template between programs.

links.title: BIP 34: Block v2, Height in Coinbase (status: Deployed)
links.why: Why the coinbase field begins with a push of the block height since 2013.

links.title: BIP 62: Dealing with malleability (status: Closed)
links.why: The attempt to forbid non-canonical encodings by consensus, which could not have solved second-party malleability.

links.title: Bitcoin Core: src/consensus/tx_check.cpp (CheckTransaction, the context-free rules)
links.why: The refusals this page names - empty inputs, empty outputs, negative or oversized amounts, duplicate inputs, a bad coinbase length - with the comment that cites the 2010 overflow bug.

links.title: Bitcoin Core: doc/bips.md (the proposals the project implements, and since which release)
links.why: Which of this chapter's standards are in the reference implementation, when each took effect, and the 28.0 note on version 3 transactions.

links.title: Transactions - Bitcoin (developer reference)
links.why: The field-by-field reference of the raw transaction format, with the compactSize table and the sequence and lock-time rules.

links.title: Bitcoin Core :: Segregated Witness Wallet Development Guide
links.why: The project's own guide to witness programs, the witness structure and transaction weight for wallet developers.

links.title: Transaction | How Bitcoin Transactions Work (learnmeabitcoin)
links.why: A drawn walk through a raw transaction's bytes, the same walk this page performs in code.

links.title: Transaction pinning | Bitcoin Optech
links.why: The attack the version 3 proposal defends against, explained for developers of contract protocols.

links.title: Replace-by-fee (RBF) | Bitcoin Optech
links.why: The history of replacement policy from the original sequence scheme to opt-in and full RBF.

links.title: Alice's transaction 46620030... on mempool.space
links.why: The explorer's record of the chapter's transaction: block 775,072, weight 569, the outpoint, the two outputs and the witness - the record this page's checks compare against.

links.title: Block 170 on mempool.space: the first transaction that spends an output
links.why: Where the chapter's first story lives: Satoshi's 10 BTC to Hal Finney, spending the coinbase of block 9.

links.title: Bitcoin: A Peer-to-Peer Electronic Cash System (the whitepaper)
links.why: The original description of a transaction as a chain of digital signatures, the first row of the chapter's table of terms.

links.title: Bitcoin Transaction Malleability and MtGox (Decker and Wattenhofer, 2014)
links.why: The measurement behind the Mt. Gox story: 302,000 BTC ever involved in malleability attacks, 1,811 before the exchange's press release.

links.title: Pizza for bitcoins? (bitcointalk, 2010)
links.why: The thread in which 10,000 BTC bought two pizzas: the 131-input transaction this page parses.

links.title: Strange block 74638 (bitcointalk, 2010)
links.why: The report of the value overflow and the five-hour timeline of the patch, as the forum recorded it.

links.title: Value overflow incident - Bitcoin Wiki
links.why: The community's account of block 74,638, the 0.3.10 fix and the reorganisation at block 74,691.

links.title: Lightning Network Explained (Wikimedia Commons, CC licence on the file page)
links.why: A short video on the payment channels that the sequence field's original scheme and BIP68's timelocks exist to make possible.

_note: Every link was fetched over HTTPS on 2026-10-08 from this session and answered 200; the title recorded here is the title the fetched document itself carries (for an improvement proposal, the Title line of its own preamble; for a web page, its <title>), not a title written from memory. A proposal's status is quoted from its preamble too, because a student needs to know whether what they are reading is deployed, draft or closed. GitHub's HTML pages answer 403 to this session's proxy, so the book chapter, the proposals and the Bitcoin Core files are linked through raw.githubusercontent.com, which answers 200 and serves the same files. YouTube answers this session with a redirect to a consent page, so no YouTube video is listed; the one video is hosted on Wikimedia Commons.
